brief: UBS sales commentary argues Defensives have run too far: Healthcare and Staples are the best 1-month sector performers, Defensives beat Cyclicals by 11% over that period, and Insurance has outperformed Banks despite weaker 3Q operational momentum. UBS reads this against a backdrop of cyclical expansion, earnings resilience and higher rates, with geopolitics (US-Iran, Russia-Ukraine, Eurozone elections) a headwind but the bar to US-Iran escalation now higher, implying a 'no war, no peace' regime where oil and rates stay structurally elevated without breaking growth. UBS prefers Healthcare (overweight, top REVS rank, half Staples' P/E-to-growth, under-owned, 2027 catalysts) over Staples (underweight, recent strength seen as a funding-trade unwind, not fundamentals). Its US/EU/EM outlooks agree earnings and growth stay resilient, valuations improved after the US derating, and favor cyclicals, capex and financials over defensives. Flows are HF/positioning-led, not LO-sponsored: US HFs covered then de-risked NVDA/AI beta; APAC saw Korean/Taiwan buying but Taiwan testing and Korean AI selling; European LOs started buying weakness. UBS's European Conference drew 1,700 investors; attendees expect debt monetization, doubt government promises, see French spreads peaking later, and flag private-credit stress, though most stay bullish US equities.
